entities.name: Our World in Data
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Our World in Data, established in 2011, is a global online platform that aggregates and visualizes data on a wide array of socio-economic issues, including health, education, and environmental sustainability. Spearheaded by researchers from the University of Oxford, particularly Hans Rosling, the initiative aims to provide accessible information that empowers people to understand and engage with the world’s most pressing challenges. Its significance lies in its commitment to evidence-based analysis, fostering informed discussions on global development and policy-making across nations.

The platform compiles a wealth of statistics from reputable sources, allowing users to explore trends over time and across different regions. It has produced detailed visualizations, such as interactive graphs and charts, that illustrate complex data in comprehensible formats. For instance, its data on global poverty reduction tracks changes from 1990 to the present, showing a dramatic decline from 36% to 9% of the world's population living on less than $1.90 a day by 2017. Such contributions not only inform public discourse but also serve as vital resources for researchers, journalists, and policymakers.

The legacy of Our World in Data is profound, as it has influenced how data journalism and public policy are approached in the digital age. By democratizing access to data and fostering transparency, it has encouraged other organizations to adopt similar methodologies, emphasizing the importance of data literacy and critical thinking. The platform's extensive dataset has been utilized in various academic works and policy drafts, thus shaping contemporary debates on sustainable development, climate change, and health crises.
